terms.comment: The classical net (Lewis & Short). Traupman gives it for “net” among his computer terms and builds interrēte on it; Andresian (p. 14) lists rēte ūniversāle among the computer words. Morgan–Owens has the heading “wireless network” with no Latin, and Levi–Bini nothing.

The international name, which Latin speakers keep as a name, as other languages do; no reference work has a Latin word for it (Morgan–Owens has the heading wifi with no entry). In the house rēte says it: Estne hīc rēte?

sources: Lewis & Short: rete
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 334.
Searched in Morgan–Owens (network, wireless network) and Levi–Bini (rete).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. wireless network, wifi (no entry).
